title: Implement the VCF Operations asynchronous report client
prompt:
The `vcfops-report` package in this repository drives the report-generation workflow of the VCF Operations API in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. Right now `src/vcfops_report/client.py` and `src/vcfops_report/cli.py` are stubs -- every method and function raises `NotImplementedError`. Implement them.

`docs/contract.json` is the authority for the wire format. It is derived from the VCF Operations OpenAPI document and names the five operations you may call -- `acquireToken`, `createReport`, `getReport`, `downloadReport` and `releaseToken` -- together with their methods, paths, Authorization header format, request-body properties and query parameters. `docs/official_sources.json` records where that document lives. Call nothing the contract does not name.

Two things the contract is strict about:

- Report generation is asynchronous. `createReport` only accepts the job; the report it hands back is not finished. Poll `getReport` until the report reaches one of the contract's terminal statuses, and download only once it has actually succeeded. Reaching the failure status has to raise rather than fall through to a download, and a report that never becomes terminal has to time out rather than poll forever.
- An optional field the caller did not set is absent from the request, not present and empty. That holds for request-body properties and for optional query parameters alike. A value the caller did set -- including a false boolean -- must be sent.

Constraints:

- Standard library only. No third-party packages.
- Keep the public API the stubs describe. The signatures, return values and exception types in the docstrings are what callers depend on. Raise the exceptions defined in `src/vcfops_report/errors.py`; do not define new ones.
- `docs/`, `mock/`, `tests/` and `verify.sh` are fixtures. Read them, do not change them.

`README.md` explains how to run the bundled loopback mock so you can exercise your implementation as you go. The mock is pinned to the same contract, explains every rejection it makes, and logs each request it receives.

Run `./verify.sh` when you are done. It must pass.

verification.notes: Starts mock/vcfops_mock.py on 127.0.0.1 and asserts the exact wire shape of every request from the mock's JSON Lines request log. No VMware endpoint is contacted.
